entities.summary: Paeonius of Ephesus was an ancient Greek architect who played a pivotal role in the construction of the magnificent temple of Artemis at Ephesus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Born in the late 5th century BCE, Paeonius was part of a team of skilled architects and engineers who worked under the patronage of the Ephesian king Croesus. The temple, completed in 356 BCE, was a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of the ancient Greeks. Its impressive size and grandeur made it a marvel of its time, attracting pilgrims and visitors from across the ancient world. Paeonius's work on the temple was later celebrated by the Roman poet Pliny the Elder, who described it as a wonder of the world. Despite its impressive legacy, Paeonius's own life and legacy remain somewhat shrouded in mystery, with few details available about his personal life or later endeavors.
